title: GRE Tunnels: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Imagine putting a letter inside a bigger envelope. The outer one carries the inner one across the network. That's a G R E tunnel.

scenes.heading: The express envelope
scenes.narration: G R E wraps packets inside new ones. It adds a four byte G R E header and a new I P header. The outer I P protocol number is forty seven. Tunnels are point to point, and can carry multicast. But G R E gives no encryption at all.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. G R E has no security. G R E is forty seven, E S P is fifty. G R E is point to point by default.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. G R E wraps packets, and adds twenty four bytes. It's I P protocol forty seven. Add I P sec if you need encryption. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva GRE lab.
